title: Shared definitions for block and decorator descriptors
description: Parameters and value expressions, shared by block-descriptor.v1.json and decorator.v1.json. The compiler contract (how each expression becomes CFEngine) is written down in blocks/README.md.

template.description: Text with {{parameter}} placeholders. As an expression it compiles to one double-quoted CFEngine string: the template's own text is written as-is, substituted values are escaped (\ -> \\, " -> \"). $(...) references are left for CFEngine to expand.

name.description: Referenced in templates as {{name}}. "value" is reserved (decorators' incoming value).

label.description: Form field label; falls back to name.

type.description: "text" is a multiline "string". "cases" is a list of condition + value rows (JSON: [{"className", "mode", "value"}]), read by cases_param. Values are stored as strings; booleans as "true"/"false".

required.description: The value must be non-empty. An optional parameter's attribute is usually wrapped in if_set, so an empty value leaves it out.

default.description: Must match `type`, and be one of `options` if those are given.

options.description: A fixed choice (select). Plain strings are value and label at once.

allowed_chars.description: Character-class fragment (as inside [...]) allowed while typing; anything else is stripped.

references.description: The value names an existing variable (autocomplete). Use it through a {"variable": ...} expression, so the compiler namespace-qualifies it.

mustache.description: Only on "text": the value is a Mustache template body (its editor inserts {{{vars.<ns>:vars.<name>}}} and {{#classes.<ns>:<name>}}).

allow_list.description: Only on "text": one value per line. Used in a promiser, the compiler emits an slist var and iterates the promise over it ($(list)); used in an expression, only through {"list_param": name}.

path.description: The value must be an absolute path (CFEngine rejects relative ones, some fatally).

expression.description: A value in compiled policy. A plain string is a quoted CFEngine string (see `template`); the objects below are everything else.

oneOf.description: A function call, e.g. readfile("/etc/x", "4096"). Numbers go in as quoted strings (CFEngine converts them; unquoted negatives don't parse).

A body reference, e.g. mog("644", "root", "root"). lib "stdlib" (masterfiles lib/, the default) compiles as default:<body>, "builder" as <file namespace>:<body>, from blocks/lib/bodies.json (the compiler writes it into the file).
A list literal from a one-value-per-line parameter (blank lines dropped).
The entry's picked classes as a list of class expressions: { "a", "!b" } (negated refs get "!"; cross-file names stay namespace-qualified). Needs at least one — and => { } is true.
A user-written class expression: quoted when it's plain (linux.!debian), emitted as-is when it's a function call (not(fileexists("/x"))).
A bundle to call (usebundle): qualified with default: when it names no namespace.

A reference to a user-picked variable, namespace-qualified by the compiler (unqualified @() and name arguments don't resolve in a namespaced file): scalar "$(ns:vars.x)", list { @(ns:vars.x) }, name "ns:vars.x" (for isvariable(), grep() ...).
Decorators only: the incoming value — the previous step's expression, nested inline. A literal list arrives as inline JSON ('["a","b"]'), a list variable as its qualified name.
Attributes only: the attribute is left out when the parameter is empty (e.g. report_to_file => "" is a hard error).
The case for the parameter's value (an options parameter): e.g. a separator per file format.
A cases parameter's rows as ifelse("<condition>", "<value>", …, <otherwise>): the first row whose condition holds wins.

A one-entry-per-line parameter (`key value` or `key=value`) as a local associative array, "<prefix><param>[key]" string => "value"; compiles to the array's qualified name, as stdlib bundles like set_line_based() take it.

Attributes only: the parameter's text, written to its own file next to the compiled policy (<block bundle>.mustache), and compiled to that file's path, "$(this.promise_dirname)/<block bundle>.mustache". The file is used as-is: no CFEngine escaping, and no $(...) expansion.
